newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Hoechst sells drug manufacturing units.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst sells drug manufacturing units.

text.p: Hoechst South Africa Ltd said on Tuesday it had sold its Aspirin, Salicylic and Methyl Salicylate businesses to Rhone-Poulenc Chimie in line with its strategy to concentrate on core operations.
The sales would take effect from March 31, 1997, it said in a statement. The sale price was not disclosed.
Hoechst said it also planned to sell its chemical manufacturing facility in Durban.
At the same time it had decided to integrate all its chemical operations into a single business unit in a bid to cut infrastructural costs.
"These changes will contribute to increased shareholder value," Hoechst said.
Hoechst in August sold its toiletries toll-manufacturing facility of its Noristan operations by means of a management buyout.
